utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may pursue, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I -- this is the first time that I see this photograph. I didn't see it before the Prosecutor showed it to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could the witness tell us where Velika and Mala Kula are located and where the fighting took place when it did. If he could just mark that by drawing circles. And that will complete my cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think this -- no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you try again, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: I think this here is Mala Kula. From this vantage point it's difficult for me to say, but I think that's it. But I can't see Velika Kula anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is that behind the ridge? That's my first question, and one more.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? What? Is what behind the ridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The Kula, where the conflict was going on. Is it behind the ridge?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And all this area here, what is the dominant feature? Could you mark the dominant feature?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the dominant feature. I might be just slightly out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine. But when you said that at the top of the ridge -- that nobody could have been on top of the ridge. So does that explain this, that anybody who went up onto the ridge would suffer the fate that you described to us?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why I said, because when there's a conflict there's crossfire. There's firing coming from various sides, bursts of gunfire. Now, who's doing the firing is difficult to assess. It's difficult for the soldiers to control this. So when the attack takes place and when there is a burst of crossfire from automatic weapons on this ridge here, well, I would never in my right mind go up on to that ridge and I don't think anybody else would either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you mark that, please. Where you -- or rather where you marked Mala Kula would you put an S and the other point would you put an R there, please. And just tell me who held this R point.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO GOJKOVIC
utterances.text: The BH army held R point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That completes my cross-examination, and I'd like to tender this photograph into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sachdeva is standing. What would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have a problem with the admission of this photograph; however, I respectfully ask leave to ask a question of the witness about his markings, because I didn't go into details about the markings in my examination in -- in my cross-examination. And in the Prosecution's submission these markings are -- well, I have some concern over these markings. It will take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, what is your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree with that. It's not in keeping with procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, you are right. It is not at all the ordinary way of proceeding, but, in fact, there are new marks on this picture, so we need to deliberate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sachdeva, the Trial Chamber believes that we've heard enough from this witness concerning that particular issue, so we're going to leave it at that. We're going to stop with the redirect of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm guided, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, you requested that this exhibit be admitted as evidence? Yes. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... D314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Registrar. Witness, this brings us to the end of your testimony. The Trial Chamber is very grateful to you for having come to The Hague to bring your contribution to the work of justice that is being done. You are now free to return home, and I'm very glad to -- happy to wish you success in the future and a good trip home. So you may now withdraw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm happy if I've managed to contribute something by my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: To be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of July, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.11 p.m.
